title: HPTLC – Bioautographic methods for selective detection of the antioxidant and α-amylase inhibitory activity in plant extracts
author: Agatonovic-Kustrin, Morton

steps.title: Prepare plant material
steps.instruction: Collect Myrmecodia platytyrea tubers, cut into small pieces, dry, and grind to a fine powder.

steps.title: Defat sample with n‑hexane
steps.instruction: Mix 800 g of the powdered plant material with n‑hexane and stir to remove fat components.

steps.title: Sequential solvent extraction
steps.instruction: Extract the defatted material sequentially with dichloromethane, then ethyl acetate, then ethanol, and finally methanol.

steps.title: Remove extraction solvents
steps.instruction: Evaporate each solvent extract using a rotary evaporator under reduced pressure at 40 °C until dry.

steps.title: Prepare final extract solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each dried extract in absolute ethanol to obtain a 1.0 mg/mL solution.

steps.title: Make stigmasterol standard
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1.0 mg/mL solution of stigmasterol in absolute ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare DPPH• radical solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve DPPH• in methanol to a concentration of 0.4 % w/v.

steps.title: Prepare anisaldehyde reagent
steps.instruction: Combine 1 mL anisaldehyde with a refrigerated mixture of glacial acetic acid, concentrated sulfuric acid, and methanol in a volume ratio of 0.5 : 50 : 1.

steps.title: Prepare α‑amylase solution
steps.instruction: Dilute approximately 1.25 mL (≈1 g) of α‑amylase liquid (Cat. No. A4862, Sigma‑Aldrich) with distilled water to a final volume of 100 mL to obtain a 1 % w/v amylase solution; store at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Scan HPTLC plates
steps.instruction: Scan developed HPTLC plates using a CAMAG TLC/HPTLC scanner 4 in automatic mode at 550 nm wavelength, with a slit width of 0.3 mm and a slit length of 4.0 mm.
